title: Watching the prompts: writing a first business prompt

units.title: Adviser demonstration with peer example
units.purpose: Demonstration phase: the adviser models construction of a fictional payment-reminder prompt live, thinking aloud and showing weak and improved versions side by side including one change that made it worse; a peer owner shows her own prompts and failures within the same phase. Choices are made visible before learners act.

corpus_citations.supported_claim: The corpus presents prompt construction as instruction plus primary content, worked basic/complex/instruction prompt examples, and best practices including being specific, clear, descriptive and using examples, which supports modelling weak versus improved prompt variants side by side.

coverage.planned_action: The adviser builds a payment-reminder prompt live, thinking aloud and showing weak and improved versions side by side, including one change that made it worse.
A peer owner shows her own prompts, failures included, within the demonstration phase.

units.title: Prompt-move annotation in pairs
units.purpose: Guided practice: participants identify prompt moves on a card and annotate a transcript in pairs, converting the demonstrated choices into concrete, identifiable moves before constructing their own prompt.

corpus_citations.supported_claim: The corpus decomposes prompts into instruction, primary content, examples, cues and templates, giving learners concrete prompt moves to identify and annotate in a transcript.

coverage.planned_action: Participants identify prompt moves on a card and annotate a transcript in pairs.

units.title: Construct a first business prompt
units.purpose: Guided practice: participants construct their own first prompt for a routine business message using fictional customer details only, applying the moves seen in the demonstration and annotation.

corpus_citations.supported_claim: The corpus describes templates with placeholders and reusable prompt libraries, supporting learners drafting a first business prompt from a repeatable structure.

coverage.planned_action: Participants construct their own first prompt for a routine business message, using fictional customer details only.

units.title: Explain two prompt choices
units.purpose: Guided practice: participants explain two choices in the prompt they constructed, making their own decisions visible rather than only watching the adviser.

corpus_citations.supported_claim: The corpus frames prompt engineering as trial-and-error with iteration and validation and domain-specific customization, supporting learners explaining and justifying their own prompt choices.

coverage.planned_action: Participants explain two choices in the prompt they constructed, rather than only watching the adviser.
